title: Distinguish large finite observation budgets from unbounded stationary sampling
statement: If every unknown stationary source column ranges over a nonempty relatively open simplex subset,any exact K protocol with a fixed finite hard cheap budgetB and at most one raw disclosure has raw probability>=1-sum_y min_x K_yx at every allowed input/channel. Multinomial Bernstein uniqueness proves it;common-part splitting attains it. For the source family the sharp value is11/40.

requires: One common algorithm exact throughout each open stationary calibration neighborhood
Fixed finite total cheap budget,including calibration observations
provides: Sharp common-part raw-read bound for every fixed hard budget
assumptions: Only Y leaves the module;private proxy records,degree,count,flags,raw values and memory are discarded.
An already-classical X persists throughout the block;coherent input or state-changing detector access is not acquired.
Not an unbounded-stopping lower bound or a lower-dimensional parametric-uncertainty theorem
costs: Charge every actual cheap/raw disclosure,calibration,preparation/reset,input lifetime,entropy,storage,latency and arithmetic. Equally informed ordinary classifiers,factories,common-part splitting and one-read caching receive the same resources. No measured complete-resource advantage.
contract.units: Dimensionless column-stochastic probabilities and total variation;cheap-call/raw-disclosure counts,internal random bits and bit operations remain separate. Physical source units,calibration,lifetime and costs require acquisition.
contract.obstruction: A nominal queried residual depends on actual L;passing several nominal inequalities does not acquire a robust implementation.
